existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: R6 `DeviceDefinition` has hard breaking changes despite retaining the same canonical identity. The top concerns are mandatory `status`, extensive path/type remodeling, and same-name semantic shifts for `url` and `version`. The main uncertainty is the lack of official cross-version ConceptMaps and narrative migration notes.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should be treated as a model transformation, not a field rename. First assign canonical metadata and lifecycle status, then convert renamed or remodeled fields (`manufacturer`, `deviceName.type`, `classification`, `deviceVersion`, `property.value[x]`, `outputLanguage`), and finally preserve R6-only or unmatched R4 content through extensions or manual review.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for structural differences because both local StructureDefinitions were present and compared directly. Confidence is medium for semantic equivalence and terminology mapping where official diffs, narrative pages, terminology expansions, and ConceptMaps were not available.

compatibilityLeverage.note: Resource-level leverage is a planning signal. It does not mark individual Revisit findings as justified or unimportant.

rationaleMd:
DeviceDefinition keeps its resource identity. The aggregate has 10 hard R4-to-R6 instance break(s), 1 potential hard break(s), 5 non-mechanical migration finding(s), and 0 direct behavior/API finding(s).

R4 maturity context is trial-use/FMM 0, which creates weak stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 100/100, producing migration shape `major-model-remodel`, major migration `Yes`, and compatibility posture `migration-program-dominates`.

11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior finding(s) are listed as context but not scored for this resource to avoid duplicating base behavior issues across all resources.
recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Plan a resource-level migration program first. Still preserve low-cost aliases, deprecated fields, wider bindings, or transition behavior for high-value Revisit findings where they reduce migration cost without perpetuating conflicting representations.

topFindings.title: DeviceDefinition.version changed from repeatable device versions to a single canonical business version
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid - R4 instances with more than one `version` fail R6 validation; semantic/API break - single values can validate while being interpreted as a different kind of version.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: deviceName.type changed from required primitive code to extensible CodeableConcept with a reduced local code system
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid - R4 primitive-code instances fail R6 structure validation, and old codes from the same complete code system may fail terminology validation or require remapping.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: manufacturer[x] was renamed and narrowed to a Reference-only manufacturer
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid - any R4 `manufacturerString` is invalid in R6, and code generators also lose the choice-type accessors.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: parentDevice, quantity, and physicalCharacteristics were removed while R6 adds different relationship and packaging structures
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid - the R4 direct elements are removed; R6-to-R4 loss/semantic loss - the new structures are not one-for-one replacements for parent, Quantity, and ProdCharacteristic data.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: specialization and capability were removed and partially replaced by conformsTo and other R6 structures
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid - R4 specialization/capability elements are removed; R6-to-R4 loss and semantic loss are possible because capability descriptions are not fully represented by `conformsTo`.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: owner, contact, and onlineInformation support fields were removed or repurposed as publisher metadata
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid - `owner` and `onlineInformation` are removed and `contact` changes type; semantic/API break - support contacts can be misread as publisher contacts.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: DeviceDefinition.type was removed and replaced by repeatable classification.type
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid - R4 instances using top-level `type` are invalid against R6 and generated APIs move the property under `classification`.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: DeviceDefinition.url was repurposed from a device network address to a canonical artifact URL
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: runtime/API/codegen - instances may pass structural validation while systems interpret an endpoint URI as a canonical artifact URL; warning-level - some old endpoint strings can trigger the new canonical URL warning.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.

topFindings.title: R6 adds mandatory DeviceDefinition.status
topFindings.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid - R4 instances without status become invalid R6 instances, and generated R6 models may require a non-null status.
topFindings.whyRelevant: Owned by this resource's StructureDefinition report.
